accident_report:
(I) Vehicle Initialization
The scenario takes place on a one-way three-lane urban arterial road with an approximate 5% uphill grade. The lanes are numbered from right to left as Lane 1, Lane 2, and Lane 3, with a continuous concrete barrier along the left side of Lane 3.
V1 is traveling in Lane 2, positioned mid-stream in traffic, with an initial speed of 60 km/h, maintaining steady following behavior and intending to continue uphill.
V2 is in Lane 2, approximately 25 m ahead of V1, with an initial speed of 58 km/h. Due to the uphill grade, its acceleration capability is limited, and it intends to maintain a steady climb.
V3 is in Lane 3, about 20 m ahead and to the left of V1, traveling at 65 km/h, maintaining a higher cruising speed.
V4 is in Lane 1, approximately 15 m behind V1, traveling at 62 km/h, maintaining stable forward motion.
(II) Scenario Development
As the vehicles continue uphill, V2 experiences reduced power performance due to the grade, and its speed gradually drops from 58 km/h to 52 km/h. This causes the gap between V1 and V2 to shrink rapidly. V1 begins mild braking, but due to delayed dynamic response on the uphill segment, it still approaches V2 at approximately 55 km/h.
Meanwhile, V3 continues in Lane 3 at a relatively higher speed and approaches the area near V1 and V2. Due to the reduced acceleration capability on the uphill, V3 misjudges its ability to pass and fails to create sufficient spacing ahead.
When the gap between V1 and V2 reduces to about 10 m, V1 initiates a lane change to Lane 3 to avoid a rear-end conflict. However, V1 does not adequately account for V3’s approach speed. V3, constrained by uphill dynamics, cannot accelerate to evade and instead performs emergency braking, reducing speed from 65 km/h to 50 km/h.
During the lane change, V1 experiences combined braking and steering inputs, reducing its lateral stability. With the concrete barrier immediately adjacent on the left side and no additional escape space, V1 is forced closer to the lane boundary under the pressure of V3’s deceleration.
(III) Outcome
Ultimately, V1 loses lateral control during the maneuver and collides with the concrete barrier on the left side of Lane 3. This first collision results from the combined effects of delayed speed adjustment due to the uphill grade, misjudged lane-change timing, and the presence of a rigid roadside obstacle. After the collision, V1 partially blocks Lane 3, forcing V3 to further decelerate and causing localized traffic disruption, though no secondary vehicle-to-vehicle collisions occur.
